data.narrative:
Carbon Robotics is a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Paul Mikesell that has raised $177M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine private companies and one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ). The three most relevant same-stage, same-sector peers—Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B)—anchor the benchmarking approach.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method applied a 1.7x multiplier to the $177M total raised, yielding an implied valuation of $301M. The peer-median method identified a $1.0B median across the three same-stage robotics comparables, with a range spanning $1.0B to $1.6B. These two approaches—capturing both capital trajectory and peer-relative positioning—converge on a three-point estimate: low of $256M, median of $650M, and high of $1.1B.

The $650M median represents a reasonable midpoint between stage-progression fundamentals and peer-market pricing, though material uncertainty remains. The wide spacing between methods ($301M versus $1.0B) reflects genuine ambiguity about whether Carbon Robotics' capital deployment, burn, and operational maturity map closer to earlier-stage funding logic or to the market valuations achieved by comparable-stage peers. Reconciling this gap requires direct assessment of unit economics, customer concentration, and path to next milestone.
